solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scored slowly

blocks.note: not a goal or a cut, but set down in a musical score
the instruction written on that score, in Italian

explanation.walkthrough: "Scored" suggests a match result, but here it means written in a musical score: ADAGIO is the tempo marking that tells players to go slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian marking on a score for a slow tempo.

clue.text: He recommends Verdi as a change

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Someone suggests swapping in some Verdi, perhaps for a change of programme at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: "as" looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser is a person who recommends a course of action.

clue.text: We can do with them

blocks.note: read literally: we are able to do things
the things we possess that make doing possible, not tools to make do with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like making do with something to hand; read literally, abilities are what allow us to do things: with them we can.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilities are the powers that let a person do things.

clue.text: Marital relations

blocks.note: gained through marriage
relatives, not intimacy

explanation.walkthrough: "Marital relations" suggests the intimate side of marriage; here the relations are relatives gained by marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: In-laws are the relatives you acquire through marriage.

clue.text: Display wines duty-free here?

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun naming the places referred to by 'here'

blocks.note: to air something is to display it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A shop shows off its wines, wondering whether they can be sold without tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the question mark: duty-free shopping is found at airports.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports are where duty-free shops are found.

clue.text: They are naturally charged for half portions

blocks.note: taken as printed, then halved

explanation.surface: Someone is billed for half portions, with a sly remark about being charged naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: "charged" tempts you toward billing; here it is electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ions are atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge.

clue.text: Urgent job for a laundress

blocks.note: needing attention now, as a matter that cannot wait
ironing clothes flat after washing

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the ironing a laundress does: pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is urgent; pressing is ironing clothes flat.

clue.text: Have fun setting up a purchase

indicators.note: In a down clue, setting a word up writes it bottom to top.

blocks.note: a purchase is a grip or leverage, and a lever gives purchase

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys arranging a shopping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: "purchase" wants to mean buying; here it is mechanical grip, which a lever provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: revelling is lively, noisy merrymaking.

clue.text: Scottish man going it alone; was he wise?

definitions.note: the question points at a person, so the definition stands for a proper noun

blocks.note: doing something alone is going solo
mon is a Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A lone Scotsman sets out on his own, and we wonder whether it was a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish man comes first in the clue but last in the answer. King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for his wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the biblical king is the proverbial model of wisdom, so the question answers itself.

clue.text: How one acts proudly but ineffectually

blocks.note: in a conceited way
to no avail, in vain

explanation.surface: Someone struts about with pride yet achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Vain has two senses: conceited, and futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting vainly is acting conceitedly, and trying vainly is trying without effect.

clue.text: Space travel in strange contrivance

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Space travel happens in some odd machine.
explanation.walkthrough: "Space travel" reads as one phrase, but "Space" is the definition on its own and "in" belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a space between two things or times.

clue.text: How one verbally passes on proverbs?

blocks.note: read the answer as two words: the means by which speech passes things on
a byword is a proverb or common saying

explanation.walkthrough: Split as BY WORDS, the answer is how one passes something on verbally; whole, a byword is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A byword is a proverb or saying in common use.

clue.text: Basic requirements for ship-launchings

blocks.note: not essentials on a list, but the physical base a ship rests on
the ramps a new hull slips down into the water

explanation.walkthrough: "Basic requirements" sounds like a checklist; literally they are the ramps at the base a ship slides down into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is the sloping ramp down which a newly built ship is launched.

clue.text: A youth initially in hovel finds refuge

blocks.note: taken as printed
first letter of youth
a hovel is squalid housing, a slum

explanation.surface: A young person living in a shack finds somewhere safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y sits inside SLUM after the S, and the A stands in front of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a political refugee seeks sanctuary, the protection a state grants.

clue.text: Caviare might produce such greed

blocks.note: an old spelling of caviar, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Expensive fish roe tempts people into gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: Caviare is an older British spelling of caviar, and its extra E is needed for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the answer leans toward a craving for money rather than food.

clue.text: Track a bird

blocks.note: a noun here: the line a train runs on
a secretive marsh bird, relative of the coot and crake

explanation.surface: Someone follows a bird's movements.
explanation.walkthrough: "Track" looks like a verb about following the bird, but it is a noun: a rail of a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: the steel bars trains run along, which stand for the whole line, and a family of wading birds.

clue.text: Gathering custom

blocks.note: a large formal meeting
an accepted way of doing things

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of one word: a large meeting, and an accepted practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plain synonyms: a conference of delegates, and an accepted practice that people follow by habit.

clue.text: Unwell, say, with bile disorder? Hard to make out

blocks.note: unwell is ill
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A patient feels ill with a liver complaint, and the diagnosis is hard to decipher.
explanation.walkthrough: "bile disorder" looks medical; the disorder is only the jumbling of B, I, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scrawled handwriting that cannot be read.

clue.text: Brave pirate’s superficial improvement

blocks.note: to brave danger is to face it
to pirate is to steal, or lift; the 's is 'is', joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A bold pirate gets a cosmetic makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: "Brave pirate" reads as adjective and noun; both are verbs here, face and lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative use: cosmetic surgery on the face, extended to any refurbishment that changes only appearances.

clue.text: Brandy’s set out for spectators

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Brandy is laid out for the audience to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: "set" reads as part of 'set out', but its letters belong to the fodder and only "out" signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: people who watch an event without taking part in it.

clue.text: Some terrible mishap results in a scar

blocks.note: the run starts at the last three letters of the first word and ends before the P of the second

explanation.surface: A nasty accident leaves someone scarred.
explanation.walkthrough: "results in" reads as cause and effect, but it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a scar is one kind of mark that spoils the skin.

clue.text: Request a slice of apple a day

blocks.note: the run skips the first two letters of apple and takes the lone a after it

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a piece of the proverbial apple a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the saying 'an apple a day keeps the doctor away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the answer carrying more urgency, like an appeal.

clue.text: The attendant’s not responsible for it

definitions.text: The attendant’s not responsible for it

blocks.note: not a staff member, but anyone who attends
someone present can't be the cause of a failure to attend

explanation.walkthrough: "attendant" suggests a museum or car-park attendant disclaiming liability; read literally, it is someone who attends, and a person who attends cannot be accounted for by absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence is failing to attend, which someone in attendance never does.

clue.text: Give up work and go to bed

blocks.note: stop working at the end of a career
withdraw for the night

explanation.surface: Someone stops working and heads off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves read as one tired person's evening; each is a separate sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to stop working for good, and also to go to bed for the night.

clue.text: Left in play

blocks.note: went away, not the opposite of right
in a stage play, where the script says Exit

explanation.walkthrough: "in play" suggests a ball game; here the play is a stage play, whose script marks departures with the stage direction Exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who has left the stage has exited.

clue.text: “Not out” the umpire is upset to conclude

blocks.note: a batter who is not out is in
a referee, or ref, is an umpire

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire is annoyed at having to rule a batter not out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter still batting is 'in' or 'not out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reach a judgement by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Measures of port take a very long time

blocks.note: Acre is an ancient port in Israel
to take ages is to take a very long time

explanation.surface: Pouring out servings of port wine is a slow business.
explanation.walkthrough: "Measures of port" reads as glasses of the wine; the port is the harbour town of Acre.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreages are areas of land measured in acres.

clue.text: Eager for silver turn-over

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to get their hands on silver that has changed hands.
explanation.walkthrough: "turn-over" looks like one word, like a business's turnover; split, it is a turn (GO) turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant.

clue.text: Break popular with those on edge

blocks.note: what is popular is in
the fringe is the people at the edge of a group

explanation.surface: A holiday that goes down well with nervous people.
explanation.walkthrough: "on edge" suggests nervous; here it is the fringe, those at the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of violating a rule, law or right.

clue.text: It gives time to see large mountain

blocks.note: large is big
ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: Someone allows enough time to visit a big mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great clock bell at the Houses of Parliament in London, and by extension its clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the famous bell strikes the hours, so the clock tower gives Londoners the time.

clue.text: Get heir a settlement he expects

definitions.note: the definition is a clause; the answer is the noun for what he expects

indicators.note: A settlement is a new arrangement, so the letters are settled into a new order.

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: An heir is told to get the legal settlement he is waiting for.
explanation.walkthrough: "settlement" reads as a legal settlement on the heir; here it is only the rearrangement of the letters, and "he" is the heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what an heir can expect to inherit.

clue.text: Strict clergyman has a setback in the diocese

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman
a bishop's see is his diocese

explanation.surface: A stern vicar suffers a reversal of fortune within his diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: "setback" suggests a misfortune; here the clergyman is literally set back.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: harsh and unbending in discipline.
